title: Absorbing Method Infrastructure for Erdos-Faudree Graphs

problemStatement.formal: Formalize edge-counting, common-neighborhood, and absorbing-pair infrastructure for Erdos-Faudree regular graphs.
problemStatement.plain: Builds the absorbing-method infrastructure around Erdos-Faudree graphs: regular edge counts, common-neighborhood bounds, absorbing triples, absorbing pairs, and a statement-level absorbing structure definition.
whyMatters: Turns the absorbing-method setup into reusable Lean graph-theory infrastructure.
Separates proved local absorbing-pair density from the still-open probabilistic machinery needed for a full absorbing lemma.

proven: regular_edge_count and erdos_faudree_edge_count prove the regular graph edge-count facts.
common_neighbors_ge and erdos_faudree_common_ge_two prove common-neighborhood lower bounds.
IsAbsorbingTriple and absorbingPairs provide the absorbing-pair framework.
absorbing_pair_exists and erdos_faudree_absorbing_pairs_ge prove local absorbing-pair existence and density.
open: Prove HasAbsorbingStructure from the local absorbing-pair infrastructure.
Formalize the probabilistic path-sampling and concentration machinery needed for a full absorbing lemma.

insights: The common-neighborhood bound is the quantitative foundation: two vertices have at least 2d - |V| common neighbors under the stated hypotheses.
For Erdos-Faudree graphs with d=n+1 and |V|=2n, the specialization gives at least two common neighbors.
The local absorbing-pair density result is proved; a full absorbing structure still needs probabilistic path-sampling and concentration machinery.
Prop-based Finset.filter keeps absorbingPairs membership proofs cleaner than Boolean filtering.
